list: A tattered curtain, smeared with bore cleaner and oil and solvent. Challenging aroma. If you can't find Paganini inside, look up—he likes to ponder while perched on the strut. Topics include philosophy, work, and tonight's supper.

A ceiling light for the workshop, second-hand. Unpretentious, and only cost Paganini one Signa Creditorum. He has staggeringly good vision, able to see things even in the dark, so this light has seldom been asked to do its job.
A plush carpet, practically of retirement age. Paganini's 'Spotless Workshop' initiative came to an abrupt halt after the dust cloud that emerged from cleaning this carpet.

A display cabinet and holy statue set. The guns are personal favorites of his. Spake Paganini to his client: 'Try them if you like, but don't touch the plant.' For while his works are many, the plants he hasn't killed are but one.
A classical and expensive lamp, the buying of which put Paganini through great mental turmoil. That said, all sense of sunk cost disappears when he sees his apprentice studying under its light.
An ornate cabinet with a recess. Furnished with holy statues and antique guns, all genuine articles from great makers. 'Veni, credidi, servavi.'

A soft, light woven rug. Pricey. Sent by a Columbian cousin on his father's side. Paganini initially mistook it as a shawl, only suspecting its ruggy nature after four whole winds around his apprentice's neck with plenty left to spare.

A simple yet stylish retro corner bench for two. Paganini sits here with his apprentice for vespers after supper. In their silent prayer, time trickles by; it makes calluses on his apprentice's fingers, and a walking stick for his knees.

A record player preloaded with hundreds of gospel tunes. The needle skips, but it still works. Whether leaving gospel on improves work efficiency, none can say; its efficacy for falling asleep at night, however, is undisputed.

Decently-maintained wooden flooring. Assembled in a lovely little geometric pattern with his apprentice long ago. Paganini can tell every floorboard individually, and every client who's ever set foot on them.
Is sanctity, too, a product of the Law?
theme: A recreation of the master gunsmith Paganini's workshop. Among the top firearm makers in Laterano, but dead last for workshop cleanliness. In the words of a client: 'The mark of quality is when you find his feathers in your barrel!'

list:
You became aware of the nature of the Law.
The Holy City still stands post-calamity, and the changing of faith is not up to its founder to decide.
During the event The Masses' Travels, obtain Operator Sankta Miksaparato

You met Patrizion at a screening of the 'Chainsaw Guy' series and became friends.
He is a gun-knight who guards the Holy City, but also an old man who has gone through all sorts of joys and sorrows.
During the event The Masses' Travels, spend 4000 Enlightened Pacifiers in [Sweet Dream Hall]

You became the most popular guest at the Shrine of Nurtury after finding so many lost baby pacifiers.
You even witnessed many of the children's halos form as they began to speak—this is when they become a 'Sankta'.
Complete all stages in [A Glance at the Shrine] with 3-star ratings (excluding tutorials)

You participated in a highly-anticipated Nativity ceremony.
It happens within dreams, but also in reality. Does it point towards a possible 'future', or to ruin...? It is yet incomplete.
Complete all the content in [Babysitting Criteria] and collect the rewards

Be it a rampaging rockhorn or a giant milk bottle spurting wildly, they will all fall into slumber under your gentle voice.
The Shrine of Nurtury has fostered innumerable creatures both living and dead, and it is no easy matter to have them share the same dream in peace. Fortunately, you can touch on their common nature.
During the event The Masses' Travels, deploy Operators on Dream Tiles a total of 20 times

Be it a snoring rockhorn or a giant milk bottle wearing a halo, they will all return to reality through your efforts.
The Shrine of Nurtury has fostered innumerable creatures both living and dead, but where Laterano should go ought to be for the Laterans to decide.
Clear MT-8 with a 3-star rating, and defeat the 'Matriarch'

The arborbeast high atop the trees grows a halo in dream, and you stay awake in the face of this wondrous sight.
Life is a wonderful thing, one that can never be measured by the confines of common sense. This you know all too well.
Complete all stages in [An Audience with God] on Challenge Mode

You witnessed a different sort of 'pilgrimage'.
It existed in the past, and happened again in the present. Then, the Sankta met the Law, and now, the Sankta define it on their own terms.
Complete all stages in [Rest in Peace] on Challenge Mode

You met a mysterious guest in the faded Holy City.
All that happened in Laterano was but the start of Terra's future.
Complete all orders from any 2 characters in [A Firearm Technician's Night] and collect the rewards

You stopped by a firearms workshop and got a hands-on lesson on how to craft a gun.
The grumpy gunsmith gives you a high rating, and the children invite you to take a photo together after obtaining their patron firearms. Their smiles are also part of your reward.
set: The Masses' Travels Engraved Medal Set

A set of engraved medals recording Laterano going through catastrophic change.
Those who travel are not just the 'saints'.
